mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant above 1.5% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 60-day return tends to be negative due to expectations of persistent higher borrowing costs compressing equity discounting.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from a zero return baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected monthly increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a labor market weakening that precedes S&P 500 declines over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month AND INDPRO < previous month
regime_hint: early signs of labor market softening
failure_condition: In 70% of such triggered windows, SPX 20-day forward returns are non-negative (p > 0.05 two-tailed test).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in home sales (HOUST) above 1.5% for three consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days as it reflects strengthening consumer confidence and demand for equity risk assets.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous month * 1.015 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 50 such triggers, the 5-day forward return mean is not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month is associated with a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days due to expectations of ongoing supply-side constraints and reduced corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: In 40% of such events, the 20-day forward return is non-negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly rises by more than 0.3% in a month with no change in FEDFUNDS, the S&P 500 forward 60-day return is likely to be negative, reflecting expectations of future inflation-driven rate hikes.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > previous month * 1.003 AND FEDFUNDS == previous month
regime_hint: unexpected inflation spike without policy easing
failure_condition: In 60% of such events, the 60-day forward return is non-negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% in a month coinciding with a monthly increase in payrolls (PAYEMS) above 20,000 suggests a strengthening labor market, which tends to drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: In 40% of such triggered windows, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in retail sales (not available in provided proxies; fallback to GDP deflator proxy via CPIAUCSL) below 105 for two consecutive months predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days due to weak consumer demand.
failure_condition: Over 30 such triggers, the 5-day forward return mean is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A double-dip in industrial production (INDPRO) contraction—first a drop of >1% then a subsequent rebound below the prior month—predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days due to persistent supply-side uncertainty and muted corporate optimism.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month * 0.99 AND INDPRO > (INDPRO two months ago)
failure_condition: In 50% of such events, the 20-day forward return is non-negative (p > 0.05).
